title: General Galois Formula: |Gal(minpoly(cos(π/n))/ℚ)| = φ(2n)/2 via IsCyclotomicExtension
description: Proves the general degree formula natDegree(minpoly ℚ (cos(π/n))) = φ(2n)/2 for all n ≥ 3 using IsCyclotomicExtension infrastructure. The key reduction is cos(π/n) = cos(2π/(2n)), allowing application of the (2n)-th cyclotomic field machinery. Answers YES to the open question: IsCyclotomicExtension is sufficient to prove the general Galois formula.

meta.author: researcher-1
meta.historicalContext: The formula |Gal(minpoly(cos(π/n))/ℚ)| = φ(2n)/2 connects classical angle trisection impossibility to cyclotomic field theory. Individual cases n=5 (|Gal|=2), n=7 (|Gal|=3), n=9 (|Gal|=3) were proved in earlier gallery entries. This file provides the general proof using IsCyclotomicExtension, answering the open question from AngleTrisectionCos20GalOQ01OQ02.
meta.proofStrategy: The key observation is cos(π/n) = cos(2π/(2n)). This reduces the problem to the cos(2π/m) family handled by AngleTrisectionOQ02OQ03OQ01 (which formalizes the (m)-th cyclotomic field machinery). Applying that infrastructure with m = 2n gives: natDegree(minpoly(cos(π/n))) = φ(2n)/2. The full Galois order = degree requires additionally showing the splitting field has degree φ(2n)/2, which follows from normality of ℚ(cos(π/n))/ℚ (conjSubgroup is normal in the abelian Galois group).

overview.problemStatement: For n ≥ 3, does the Galois group of the minimal polynomial of cos(π/n) over ℚ have order φ(2n)/2? Can this be proved using IsCyclotomicExtension?
overview.historicalContext: The connection between cos(π/n) and cyclotomic fields goes back to Gauss's Disquisitiones Arithmeticae (1801) §VII, where Gauss explicitly computed which regular n-gons are constructible by reducing the question to the splitting behavior of cyclotomic polynomials and proving that the n-th cyclotomic field has degree φ(n) over ℚ. The angle-trisection consequence — that an angle θ can be trisected by compass and straightedge iff cos(θ/3) lies in a tower of degree-2 extensions of ℚ(cos θ) — was made precise by Pierre Wantzel (1837) in 'Recherches sur les moyens de reconnaître si un Problème de Géométrie peut se résoudre avec la règle et le compas', the first paper to rigorously prove the impossibility of angle trisection (alongside doubling the cube). Wantzel's argument is exactly that cos(20°) = cos(π/9) satisfies the irreducible cubic 8x³ − 6x − 1 = 0, so [ℚ(cos 20°):ℚ] = 3, which is not a power of 2. The general statement |Gal(minpoly(cos(π/n))/ℚ)| = φ(2n)/2 follows from Galois theory of cyclotomic fields: ℚ(cos(π/n)) = ℚ(ζ_{2n})⁺ (the maximal real subfield, fixed field of complex conjugation), with Galois group (ℤ/2nℤ)×/{±1} of order φ(2n)/2. The minimal polynomials are essentially Chebyshev-like polynomials closely related to Lucas sequences (Lehmer 1933 worked these out explicitly). Gallery entries had previously verified n=5,7,9 case-by-case; this file provides the uniform IsCyclotomicExtension proof using Mathlib's full cyclotomic theory infrastructure.
keyInsights: cos(π/n) = cos(2π/(2n)): This arithmetic identity is the central reduction. It connects the cos(π/n) family to the cos(2π/m) family (with m = 2n), for which AngleTrisectionOQ02OQ03OQ01 provides complete formalization.

natDegree(minpoly(cos(π/n))) = φ(2n)/2: FULLY PROVED. Apply minpoly_alphaCos_natDegree from AngleTrisectionOQ02OQ03OQ01 with m = 2n, using NeZero (2n) and the cosine identity. This is the central mathematical content.

ℚ(cos(π/n)) is Galois over ℚ: The maximal real subfield of CyclotomicField(2n,ℚ) is the fixed field of the complex conjugation automorphism σ (ζ_{2n} ↦ ζ_{2n}^{-1}). Since the Galois group (ℤ/2nℤ)× is abelian, every subgroup (including ⟨σ⟩) is normal, so the fixed field is Galois over ℚ.

Splitting field = ℚ(cos(π/n)): By normality, minpoly(cos(π/n)) splits completely over ℚ(cos(π/n)). Since ℚ(cos(π/n)) is generated by one root, SplittingField ≅ ℚ(cos(π/n)), giving finrank SplittingField = φ(2n)/2.

Constructibility consequence (Wantzel's theorem): a regular n-gon is compass-straightedge constructible iff [ℚ(cos(2π/n)):ℚ] is a power of 2, equivalently iff φ(n) is a power of 2 (i.e., n is of the form 2^k · (product of distinct Fermat primes)). The same constructibility criterion applied to cos(π/n) gives the angle-trisection impossibility: trisecting θ requires constructing cos(θ/3), and 60° trisection asks for cos(20°), whose minimal polynomial 8x³−6x−1 has degree 3, not a power of 2. The Galois order formula φ(2n)/2 makes this constructibility analysis uniform across all n.
overview.proofStrategy: Step 1 (trivial): Prove cos(π/n) = cos(2π/(2n)) by arithmetic. Step 2 (main): Apply AngleTrisectionOQ02OQ03OQ01's minpoly_alphaCos_natDegree and minpoly_alphaCos_eq_minpoly_cos with m = 2n to get natDegree = φ(2n)/2. Step 3 (complete): Show SplittingField has degree φ(2n)/2 via normality of ℚ(cos(π/n))/ℚ — uses autEquivPow isomorphism showing conjSubgroup is normal in the abelian Galois group (IsCyclic.card_pow_eq_one_le), then IsSplittingField.lift for the upper bound and AdjoinRoot lower bound via omega.

sections.title: §1. The Cosine Identity: cos(π/n) = cos(2π/(2n))
sections.summary: cos_pi_eq_cos_2pi_div_2n: proves the arithmetic identity cos(π/n) = cos(2π/(2n)) for n ≥ 1 by `congr 1; push_cast; ring`. This is the key reduction connecting the cos(π/n) family to the cos(2π/m) family with m = 2n.
sections.mathContext: $\cos(\pi/n) = \cos(2\pi/(2n))$: algebraic rewriting of $\pi/n = 2\pi/(2n)$ using `push_cast` and `ring`. Simple arithmetic, but crucial for applying the cyclotomic field machinery which is stated for $\cos(2\pi/m)$.

sections.title: §2. Degree Theorem (Sorry-Free)
sections.summary: cos_pi_minpoly_natDegree: natDegree(minpoly ℚ (cos(π/n))) = φ(2n)/2 for n ≥ 3. Proof: rewrite cos(π/n) as cos(2π/(2n)) using sec-cosine-identity, then apply AngleTrisectionOQ02OQ03OQ01.minpoly_alphaCos_natDegree with m = 2n.
sections.mathContext: $\text{natDegree}(\text{minpoly}\ \mathbb{Q}\ (\cos(\pi/n))) = \varphi(2n)/2$. Uses `haveI : NeZero (2*n)` to satisfy the cyclotomic field instances, then `minpoly_alphaCos_eq_minpoly_cos` to transfer to `alphaCos`, then `minpoly_alphaCos_natDegree` from the parent file.

sections.title: §3. Extension Degree (Sorry-Free)
sections.summary: cos_pi_extension_degree: ∃ K ⊆ ℝ, cos(π/n) ∈ K ∧ [K:ℚ] = φ(2n)/2. Proved by instantiating K = maxRealSubfield (CyclotomicField (2n) ℚ) and applying the rank formula.
sections.mathContext: The intermediate field $K = \mathbb{Q}(\cos(2\pi/(2n)))^+ = $ maxRealSubfield of $\text{CyclotomicField}(2n, \mathbb{Q})$ has $[K:\mathbb{Q}] = \varphi(2n)/2$ by the real embedding degree theorem.

sections.title: §4. Splitting Field Degree
sections.summary: cos_pi_splitting_finrank: finrank ℚ (SplittingField (minpoly ℚ (cos(π/n)))) = φ(2n)/2 — fully proved (0 sorries). Closes the previously documented sorry inline via 7 sub-steps (§A-§G) covering: abelian Galois group via autEquivPow, conjSubgroup normality, finrank of maxRealSubfield, alphaCos identification, Normal.splits to lift minpoly, IsSplittingField.lift for the upper bound, exists_root_of_splits + AdjoinRoot for the lower bound, and `omega` to close.
sections.mathContext: Two-sided finrank bound: upper bound $\leq \varphi(2n)/2$ via $\text{SplittingField} \hookrightarrow F$ (IsGalois ensures minpoly splits over $F$); lower bound $\geq \varphi(2n)/2 = \text{natDegree}(p)$ via $\text{AdjoinRoot}(p) \hookrightarrow \text{SplittingField}$ using a root from `exists_root_of_splits`. Closed by `omega`.

sections.title: §5. Galois Group Order
sections.summary: cos_pi_gal_card: |Gal(minpoly ℚ (cos(π/n)))| = φ(2n)/2. Follows from Polynomial.Gal.card_of_separable (which gives |Gal(p)| = finrank(SplittingField)) and the splitting field degree. The companion gal_order_eq_totient_div2_general is the public-facing restatement.
sections.mathContext: `Polynomial.Gal.card_of_separable`: for separable $p$, $|\text{Gal}(p)| = [\text{SplittingField}(p):\mathbb{Q}]$. Combined with $\text{finrank}\ \text{SplittingField} = \varphi(2n)/2$, this gives the Galois group order.

sections.title: §6. Consistency Checks for n=5,7,9
sections.summary: Verifies the general formula φ(2n)/2 against the three known special cases: n=5 (φ(10)/2=2), n=7 (φ(14)/2=3), n=9 (φ(18)/2=3). All consistent with previously proved gallery entries.
sections.mathContext: Spot checks: $\varphi(10)/2 = \varphi(2\cdot 5)/2 = 4/2 = 2$ ✓; $\varphi(14)/2 = 6/2 = 3$ ✓; $\varphi(18)/2 = 6/2 = 3$ ✓. These match the specific entries AngleTrisectionCos20GalOQ01OQ02 (n=5,7) and AngleTrisectionCos20Gal (n=9).

conclusion.summary: The open question is answered YES: IsCyclotomicExtension is sufficient to prove the general Galois formula |Gal(minpoly(cos(π/n))/ℚ)| = φ(2n)/2. Both the degree theorem natDegree(minpoly ℚ (cos(π/n))) = φ(2n)/2 and the Galois order result |Gal| = φ(2n)/2 are fully proved (0 sorries, 0 axioms). The key steps are: (1) cos(π/n) = cos(2π/(2n)) reduction; (2) cyclotomic degree formula from AngleTrisectionOQ02OQ03OQ01; (3) normality of conjSubgroup via autEquivPow isomorphism (abelian Galois group); (4) splitting field finrank pinched between AdjoinRoot lower bound and maxRealSubfield upper bound.
conclusion.implications: This entry provides the uniform proof of the Galois formula across all n ≥ 3, replacing case-by-case computations with a single IsCyclotomicExtension argument. The formula φ(2n)/2 shows precisely which cos(π/n) values are constructible (degree 1 or 2) vs. non-constructible (degree ≥ 3), directly formalizing angle trisection impossibility for all relevant n.
openQuestions: Is there a cleaner proof of cos_pi_gal_card that avoids the splitting-field detour, working directly with the maximal real subfield of CyclotomicField(2n,ℚ)?
Can the formula be generalized to |Gal(minpoly(cos(kπ/n))/ℚ)| for other rational multiples kπ/n, or to other trigonometric values like sin(π/n)?

references.title: Wantzel, P. L., 'Recherches sur les moyens de reconnaître si un Problème de Géométrie peut se résoudre avec la règle et le compas' (1837)
references.description: First rigorous proof of the impossibility of angle trisection and cube duplication. Establishes the field-theoretic constructibility criterion (degree must be a power of 2) and applies it to cos(20°).

references.title: Lehmer, D. H., 'A note on trigonometric algebraic numbers' (Amer. Math. Monthly, 1933)
references.description: Explicit minimal polynomials and recursion identities for cos(2π/n) and related Chebyshev-Lucas sequences. The polynomials computed here are exactly the ones whose Galois groups this entry formalizes.
